science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,300 K and log g 4.51 (u1 0.573, u2 0.184): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Sector 4
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 10.2 days, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 4 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 0.76%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.14%, the light's own noise being 0.04%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. Canto Martins et al. (2020, ApJS 250, 20) list the star as a rotator in their table (VizieR J/ApJS/250/20, table 1): a rotation period of 10.229 ± 1.217 d, the peak of the wavelet's global spectrum of 43 days of the star's light in sectors 1 to 22 (4.2 cycles), which the paper lists among its unambiguous rotation periods. The rotation and its period are theirs, taken as published; no criteria were applied to them here. The map is made at a tilt of 46°, worked out from the star's rotation speed, period and radius. Gaia DR3 lists 3 other stars within 63 arcseconds, with 14% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 4

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffe9da, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 5 (November and December 2018): the map's scale, 92% to 108% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 11.3% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · November and December 2018
